bihar_raw_news.title: Nepal flash flood may swell Gandak; NDRF deploys 20 teams in Bihar , UP - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 26, 2026 Nepal flash flood may swell Gandak; NDRF deploys 20 teams in Bihar, UP Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Source: PTI The NDRF on Wednesday said it is on "high alert" in the eventuality of flash floods in Nepal causing water levels to surge in the Gandak river and inundate border areas of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. In an updated statement at 6:30 pm, the federal continency force said it was keeping a "close watch" on the situation and has deployed 20 teams for flood rescue operations in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. It said an advisory issued by the Central Water Commission (CWC) apart from media reports state that a sudden rise in river water level in the Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal has taken place, around 160 km from the Indian border, due to suspected Glacial Lake Outburst Floor (GLOF) activity near the Nepal-China border. "The flood wave is likely to travel downstream in the Gandak river. Local authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh near the India-Nepal border along the Gandak river have been advised to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the situation," the force said. Keeping in view the anticipated floods in the Gandak river due to the flash flood incident in Nepal, NDRF is on high alert, it said. The statement added that NDRF has deployed nine teams in Bihar including in the West Champaran and Muzaffarnagar districts apart from 11 teams in Uttar Pradesh which includes Kushinagar district, likely to be impacted due to its close vicinity to the Gandak river. "NDRF, in close coordination with the state governments of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh and the CWC, is keeping a close watch on the situation. "Additional teams are on standby for emergent requirements in case of any unforeseen situation," it said. Officials told PTI that a few teams of NDRF rescuers have been kept in readiness to be airlifted to Nepal from the Indian Air Force (IAF) station in Ghaziabad once the government of Nepal seeks assistance for such a manpower from India. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Unveils ₹70,000-Crore Plan for 126-km Ganga Marine Drive - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Bihar Unveils ₹70,000-Crore Plan for 126-km Ganga Marine Drive 26 Aug 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a major infrastructure plan to expand Patna’s J.P. Ganga Path into a 126-km Ganga Marine Drive . The proposed project involves an estimated investment of ₹70,000 crore , comprising ₹20,000 crore from the state government and ₹50,000 crore through private investment . Key Points: Project: The proposed Ganga Marine Drive will involve the expansion of J.P. Ganga Path over a distance of 126 km . Location: The project will be developed along the Ganga River in Bihar , with the existing J.P. Ganga Path serves as its foundation. Estimated Investment: The project is expected to involve an investment of approximately ₹70,000 crore . State Government Contribution: Around ₹20,000 crore has been proposed to be invested by the Bihar Government . Private Investment: Approximately ₹50,000 crore is proposed to be mobilised through private investment . Infrastructure Development: The project aims to strengthen road connectivity and transport infrastructure along the Ganga corridor. Employment Generation: The initiative is expected to create employment opportunities through infrastructure construction and associated economic activities. Economic Growth: The project is intended to attract private investment, promote commerce and support regional economic development . J.P. Ganga Path: It is a major road infrastructure project along the southern bank of the Ganga in Patna , designed to improve connectivity within the city and its surrounding areas. Public-Private Participation: The proposed financing model reflects an effort to combine government resources with private-sector investment for large-scale infrastructure development. Significance: The proposed Ganga Marine Drive could strengthen Bihar’s transport infrastructure and economic connectivity along the Ganga corridor. bihar_raw_news.title: SC appoints ex-chief justice of Orissa HC as administrator of Bihar Cricket Association
bihar_raw_news.content: SC appoints ex-chief justice of Orissa HC as administrator of Bihar Cricket Association A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan took note of a report filed by former apex court judge Justice L Nageswara Rao, who was appointed as the ombudsman of the BCA in August last year. By PTI August 26, 2026, 7:29:55 PM IST (Published) 3 Min Read The Supreme Court has appointed former chief justice of the Orissa High Court Justice Chakradhari Sharan Singh to act as an administrator of the Bihar Cricket Association (BCA). A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan took note of a report filed by former apex court judge Justice L Nageswara Rao, who was appointed as the ombudsman of the BCA in August last year. The bench, which said the report was "quite exhaustive", noted the conclusion and final recommendations of the report. It said in the recommendations, the ombudsman has suggested that an administrator be appointed and he be tasked with conducting a verification exercise across all district cricket associations (DCAs). The bench noted the ombudsman has also made recommendations concerning fresh elections. In its recommendations, the ombudsman has said, "Several discrepancies pertaining to the electoral college have been enumerated above. In light thereof, the elections of BCA conducted in 2025 cannot be deemed to having been conducted freely and fairly". The ombudsman has recommended that after the administrator completes the task of verification of DCA clubs, the BCA's electoral college should be recalibrated and elections to the DCAs and BCA should be conducted in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the BCA and the various DCAs. "In view of the aforesaid, we appoint Justice Chakradhari Sharan Singh, former Chief Justice of the Orissa High Court, to act as an administrator of the Bihar Cricket Association," the top court said in its August 20 order. "The administrator shall proceed further in accordance with what has been recommended by the ombudsman as contained in paragraph 91 (about fresh elections) of the recommendations, referred to above," it said. The bench noted there were some objections insofar as the ombudsman's report was concerned, and it would look into it at an appropriate time. "As an interim measure, we direct that the recommendations shall come into force forthwith and be implemented," it said. The bench, which was dealing with a matter related to the BCA, posted it for further hearing on October 8. In August last year, it had appointed Justice Rao as the ombudsman of the BCA and requested him to have a formal meeting with the stakeholders and try to workout the modalities for smooth functioning of the association. In its March 20 order, the top court had noted that Justice Rao had forwarded his exhaustive report along with a separate note. bihar_raw_news.title: "Empowered women will shape Bihar's future": CM Samrat Chaudhary launches initiatives ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "Empowered women will shape Bihar's future": CM Samrat Chaudhary launches initiatives for safety, education and entrepreneurship ANI | Updated: Aug 26, 2026 17:37 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], August 26 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Wednesday launched three initiatives aimed at strengthening women's safety, education and self-reliance on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, saying empowered women will play a key role in building a developed Bihar . Addressing an event at Gyan Bhawan in Patna, the Chief Minister inaugurated and flagged off 4,700 scooters and motorcycles for women police personnel under the 'Police Didi (Abhaya Brigade)' initiative. CM Chaudhary said the vehicles will enable women police personnel to work more effectively in ensuring the safety of girls and women, especially in schools and colleges. "Women's increasing participation is a sign of a prosperous Bihar . The government aims to ensure that women contribute significantly to the state's development through their talent and capabilities," he said. The Chief Minister also launched the 'Mukhyamantri Balika PhD Fellowship' scheme, under which nearly 1,000 girl students will receive financial assistance of Rs 10,000 per month for four years to pursue higher studies and research. He further launched the ' Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme' to promote women entrepreneurship. Under the scheme, 2,100 women entrepreneurs will be provided financial assistance ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh for their innovative ideas and ventures. Highlighting the role of women in Bihar 's economy, CM Chaudhary said 43 lakh Jeevika Didis have become 'Lakhpati Didis' and women self-help groups are making a significant contribution to the state's economic growth. He added that the government aims to connect one crore women with employment and self-employment opportunities, including Jeevika, dairy production and animal husbandry. The Chief Minister also said emergency service 112 has improved its response time to less than 10 minutes, with a target to bring it down further to 5-7 minutes for providing quick assistance to citizens. CM Chaudhary said the government is committed to creating a safe and enabling environment for women and ensuring their participation in the mainstream of development. Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, ministers, senior officials, police officers and women personnel of the Abhaya Brigade were present during the programme. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Nepal flash flood: Bihar on high alert over possible Gandak river water level surge
bihar_raw_news.content: Nepal flash flood: Bihar on high alert over possible Gandak river water level surge (Photo: IANS) India 26th August 2026 Patna, August 26 (IANS): The Bihar government on Wednesday intensified flood preparedness across districts along the Gandak river following warnings of a possible flash-flood wave in the river's upper catchment area in Nepal. Preliminary assessments indicate that a flood wave of around three metres could potentially reach the Gandak, prompting authorities to place several districts on high alert. A high-level review meeting chaired by Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit was held on Wednesday, with District Magistrates, senior police officers and Superintendents of Police from vulnerable districts joining via video conference. The meeting reviewed the situation in Nepal and its possible impact on Bihar. The Chief Secretary directed officials to ensure that rescue, evacuation and relief arrangements are completed in advance and that people can be moved to safer locations immediately if river levels rise suddenly. Special vigilance has been ordered in West Champaran (Bettiah), East Champaran (Motihari), Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur, and Vaishali. Authorities in Sitamarhi and Sheohar, along with other vulnerable districts, have also been instructed to maintain continuous monitoring. Officials have been directed to regularly inspect river levels, embankments, low-lying areas, bridges, culverts and other vulnerable infrastructure and immediately report any signs of damage or stress. The state has begun pre-deploying additional emergency resources. An NDRF team is being sent to Gopalganj, while another will remain on standby in Muzaffarpur. Arrangements are also being made to deploy an NDRF team to Bettiah within nearly two hours. The Sashastra Seema Bal Deputy Inspector General Sanjay Singhal has assured the availability of Quick Reaction Teams (QRTs) and other assistance in Bettiah if required. Districts have also been instructed to keep adequate numbers of boats, relief shelters and community kitchens ready so that evacuation and relief operations can begin without delay. The Water Resources Department has been directed to ensure safe management of water through the Gandak Barrage and its canal system. Engineers and other officials have been told to maintain constant vigilance and conduct regular inspections of embankments and critical water infrastructure. Within the Gandak catchment, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Lamjung and Tanahun in Nepal have been identified as high-risk areas. Dolakha and Sindhupalchok have been classified as high-risk zones in the Kosi catchment, while moderate risks have been forecast in several areas of the Kosi, Bagmati and Gandak catchments. The Bihar government has emphasised that there is no need for panic, but residents in vulnerable areas should remain alert and follow instructions issued by local authorities. District Magistrates have been asked to conduct daily media briefings and monitor social media to counter rumours and misinformation. Residents have been urged to rely only on official and credible sources for flood-related information.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar on high alert as Nepal flash floods raise Gandak River surge risk
bihar_raw_news.content: Edited By : Anand P Last Updated: 26 August 2026, 04:52 PM IST Share At least 105 Indian tourists are among 291 foreign nationals reported missing after the flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa area A woman looks on as the floodwater flows in spate across a residential area in Nepal | PTI Patna: Bihar has stepped up vigilance and preparedness measures as deadly flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa region left people dead and hundreds of foreign nationals, including Indians, reported missing, raising concerns over a possible sudden surge in the Gandak River. The Bihar Disaster Management Department said special monitoring was being maintained following the emergence of a flash-flood situation in the upper catchment of the Gandak River in Nepal and the possibility of a sharp increase in water flow downstream. At least 105 Indian tourists are among 291 foreign nationals reported missing after the flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa area, according to the Nepal Tourism Board. The missing foreign nationals also include 17 Malaysians, 12 Britons, four South Africans, three Americans, one Australian and one Dutch national. The nationalities of another 103 missing people are yet to be confirmed. The sudden flooding has affected areas near the Nepal-Tibet border, with Timure and Syafrubesi in Rasuwa among the worst-hit locations. Four bodies -- three men and a woman -- were also recovered from Nuwakot district following the disaster, according to Nepalese authorities. Against this backdrop, Bihar authorities have warned of a potential flash-flood risk in districts along the Gandak River and directed officials to keep rescue and relief arrangements ready. "A high risk of flash floods is forecast for the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Lamjung, and Tanahun districts (Gandak catchment) and the Dolakha and Sindhupalchok districts (Kosi catchment) in Nepal," the Disaster Management Department said. Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit chaired a high-level review meeting on Wednesday, attended through video conferencing by District Magistrates and senior police officials, including Superintendents of Police, from the districts concerned. Officials reviewed the evolving situation and were instructed to maintain heightened vigilance and ensure that all preparedness measures for rescue and relief operations remained in place. The Water Resources Department has also directed officials to release water through all gates of the Gandak Barrage and its associated canals to manage the available water flow safely and effectively. Water resources officials and engineers have been asked to maintain round-the-clock vigilance in their respective areas and closely monitor critical infrastructure, including embankments. Authorities in Bihar are continuing to track developments in Nepal and the resulting water levels in the Gandak system as they prepare for any sudden rise in downstream flows. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar schoolgirls turn Raksha Bandhan into a call for safer schools, raise concerns
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Education Today News Bihar schoolgirls turn Raksha Bandhan into a call for safer schools, raise concerns Bihar schoolgirls turn Raksha Bandhan into a call for safer schools, raise concerns A Raksha Bandhan celebration at the Dhanbad Collectorate turned into an open discussion on school infrastructure and girls' safety. Schoolgirls tied rakhis to senior officials and spoke directly about problems they face in and around their schools. advertisement Bihar schoolgirls turn Raksha Bandhan into a call for safer schools, raise concerns Sithun Modak Dhanbad, UPDATED: Aug 26, 2026 14:19 IST Edited By: Princy Shukla Raksha Bandhan took a different turn at the Dhanbad Collectorate this year when schoolgirls from government schools tied rakhis to senior district officials and then used the occasion to speak about problems affecting their schools. The students tied handmade rakhis to officials, including the Deputy Commissioner and Senior Superintendent of Police, highlighting the traditional brother-sister bond. But the interaction soon moved beyond the festival as students spoke about damaged school buildings, missing basic facilities and safety concerns on their way to school. advertisement Read More The officials listened to the students and assured them that the concerns raised would be looked into. RAKHIS, THEN REAL QUESTIONS The students' handmade rakhis became part of an interaction that gave them a direct platform to speak to the district administration. Some students pointed to infrastructure problems, including classrooms, boundaries and playgrounds that need attention. Others raised concerns about harassment and eve-teasing while travelling to school. The administration said several civil works are already at the tender or estimation stage and that work is expected to progress over the coming months. Aditya Ranjan, Deputy Commissioner of Dhanbad, said the purpose of the interaction was to understand what was actually happening in schools rather than relying only on official files. “The correct proof of our work is not in the files. It is in the work happening in the schools, in the satisfaction of the teachers and the children.” advertisement 1,000 SCHOOLS IN FOCUS The district administration is working on civil works in around 500 schools, while another 500 schools are being considered for facilities such as benches and desks, musical instruments and computers. The administration's larger plan is to develop government schools towards the standard of CM School of Excellence, with a focus on giving rural students facilities similar to those available in private schools. Ranjan said the interaction helped officials identify problems that they were not previously aware of. He added that the administration would focus on addressing shortcomings across around 1,750 schools in the district, with the aim of ensuring that government-school students have a better learning environment. POLICE TO PATROL SCHOOLS Girls also raised safety concerns, particularly about harassment and unwanted attention while travelling to school. Following the concerns, the Senior Superintendent of Police announced that police stations would conduct regular patrolling around schools and check the surroundings. Ranjan said the administration expects visible changes on the ground over the next six months. - Ends Published By:

In a social media post, Mr Radhakrishnan conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He also prayed for the safe and swift rescue of all those who are missing. Mr Radhakrishnan said that the thoughts of the people of India are with the people of Nepal during this difficult hour. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time. He said, India is ready to provide all possible humanitarian assistance to Nepal. The Prime Minister said, our teams are coordinating closely on rescue and relief efforts. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for assistance and information regarding Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Nepal today. The Embassy said that people requiring assistance can contact the embassy on helpline +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500. The Embassy said, it has remained engaged with the relevant authorities of Government of Nepal for early rescue and relief for Indian nationals affected by the flash floods. It said, rescue and relief efforts continue to be strengthened in coordination with the Government of Nepal. According to the official sources, India is preparing to send relief material as soon as possible to Nepal. The Tamil Nadu Government has announced a help desk for tourists from Tamil Nadu who have gone to visit Nepal. The Government has appealed to get in touch with the help desk and the State Department for Overseas Affairs. It said that help can also be sought from the Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi. national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 38 Nepal flash floods leave 384 tourists missing, including 105 Indians
national_raw_news.content: More than 100 Indians are among 384 tourists reported missing in Nepal after flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River hit the Rasuwa region near the Tibet border this morning. According to the Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) the 384 missing tourists include 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali citizens. It said, the foreign nationals are from several countries, including 105 from India, and others from the United Kingdom, Australia, the United States, Malaysia, South Africa and the Netherlands. However, the NTB clarified that the figures are preliminary and are currently being verified and cross-checked with travel agencies, local authorities and other concerned agencies. According to local media reports, seven people have died following the massive flash flood. Preliminary information suggests that the flash flood was caused by an earthquake triggering an avalanche with melted snow pouring into the Bhote Koshi river. The flash floods in the Bhote Koshi River caused a major disruption in the Rasuwa region, triggering concerns over the safety of tourists and other people present in the affected areas. Authorities and rescue agencies are continuing efforts to assess the situation and establish the whereabouts of those reported missing. The Nepal Tourism Board has also issued emergency contact numbers for tourists and their families seeking information or assistance. The emergency contacts include the toll-free number 1234, the hotline 1144 and the Tourist Police number 9851289445. The tourism board urged tourists in the affected areas to remain calm, stay informed through official channels and follow all safety instructions issued by the authorities. In view of the situation, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah has consulted with federal parliamentarians from the affected areas, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan. The discussion focused on the damage caused by the flash flood, the condition of coastal settlements, and rescue and relief efforts. Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah had convened a meeting of the National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management to review the situation in the flood-affected areas and the progress of rescue, search and relief efforts. Search and rescue operations are underway, and further details are awaited.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Regional News 10 Bihar steps up flood preparedness amid possibility of rise in Gandak River
national_raw_news.content: Bihar has stepped up flood preparedness following flash floods in Nepal and the possibility of a sudden rise in the water level of the Gandak River. Six districts of the state – West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali – have been placed under heightened vigilance along the Gandak river system. Besides, District Magistrates of Sitamarhi, Sheohar and other districts have also been directed to keep a close and continuous watch on the situation. People living in low-lying areas of Bagaha in West Champaran and Vaishali district have been urged to move to safer places at the earliest. In view of the possibility of increased water flow in the Gandak River, an NDRF team has been deployed in Gopalganj and Bettiah, while another team has been kept on standby in Muzaffarpur. Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary said that a high-level team has been constituted to closely monitor the situation. In view of the situation, a high-level review meeting was held today in Patna under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit. District Magistrates and senior police officials of the concerned districts have been directed to maintain round-the-clock surveillance and keep rescue and relief arrangements on standby. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also spoke to Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary over the phone in view of the flood threat in Bihar due to torrential rain and glacier burst in Nepal. Home Minister assured the state government of providing all possible assistance to deal with the emerging situation. Mr Shah added that National Disaster Response Force is being mobilised to deal with the situation.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 150 FM Nirmala Sitharaman says India’s transformation is structural, driven by rapid urbanisati...
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India stands as the fastest-growing major economy in the world and offers a unique combination of scale, sustained growth, a young population, expanding consumption and rapidly deepening capital markets. Addressing prominent members of the Indian business community in Toronto today, Sitharaman said India’s transformation is structural, driven by rapid urbanisation, a growing middle class and world-class digital infrastructure. She noted that these developments are creating new opportunities across virtually every sector of the economy. The Finance Minister also highlighted the role of India’s digital ecosystem in transforming access to financial and commercial services. She underlined significant opportunities for collaboration with Canadian banks, fintech companies and regulators, not only in payments but also in shaping the next generation of digital financial infrastructure. Highlighting the growing India-Canada economic partnership, Sitharaman said the Indian diaspora in Canada serves as a strategic bridge between the two countries. She said India-Canada bilateral ties have undergone a remarkable transformation in recent times, supported by shared democratic and pluralistic values, expanding economic engagement, high-level interactions and strong people-to-people ties. Referring to the agreement reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Canadian counterpart Mark Carney on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in June 2025 to reset bilateral ties, Sitharaman said the two countries have reaffirmed their commitment to building a future-focused strategic partnership. Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman arrived in Toronto yesterday for a four-day official visit to Canada, focused on strengthening bilateral trade, investment linkages and financial cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: Delhi Government hands over approval letters to 4,000 women under Lakshmi Yojana 31 mins ago 14
national_raw_news.content: The Delhi Government today handed over the approval letters to the 4 thousand eligible women beneficiaries under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana out of which 2 thousand 500 letter given at the formal ceremony. Under the scheme, eligible women will receive financial assistance of 2 thousand 500 rupees every month. Speaking on the occasion, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu said that this initiative is a significant step towards women’s welfare, empowerment, and dignity. He also highlighted the importance of empowering women and ensuring their rightful place in the social and economic development of the nation. Our correspondent reports that the monthly assistance will strengthen financial security, everyday choice and self-reliance. The Delhi Government has finalised the manner in which the assistance can be disbursed. Eligible women will receive one thousand rupees every month through a digital wallet and one thousand 500 rupees will be deposited as a fixed deposit, with interest to be borne by the government. Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that this initiative is a significant step towards women’s welfare, empowerment and dignity. She added that this financial assistance can help women meet important needs, including children’s care and education, household requirements or support for their livelihood and business activities. Around nine lakh thirteen thousand women registered for the scheme and over six lakh 52 thousand applications were submitted. The Delhi government said that the financial assistance will be credited directly to women beneficiary’s bank accounts from 1st of next month. A financial outlay of five thousand one hundred 10 crore rupees has been made for the scheme in the 2026-27 Delhi Budget. The response to the scheme reflects the confidence Delhi’s women have placed in this initiative and strengthens the Government’s resolve to widen opportunity and empowerment across the capital.
